nodes.question: Compare the source and edited images. Identify the original blue mug by its visual appearance and handle, and determine whether that same mug moved relative to the headphones. If multiple mugs appear, distinguish the original from added mugs; if identity cannot be established, report unknown.
nodes.criteria: Complete only if the source blue mug is identifiable in the edited image and that same mug is now to the right of the headphones. Partial if the original mug has moved toward the right but has not reached the right side. Absent if the original mug shows no progress toward the right. A newly added mug on the right does not count as movement or progress. Use unknown if the original mug's identity or displacement cannot be established from the images.
nodes.binding: Original blue ceramic mug with a handle, located left of the black over-ear headphones in the source image; track this same mug across source and edited images. Headphones are the black over-ear headphones.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
